data.title: Pre-decoded + pre-resized rbb frames at 256² uint8
data.summary: Precompute the per-shot uint8 RGB 256×256 frame tensor once and store it next to the raw Zarr. Saves the uint16→uint8 normalisation and the 536×560→256×256 bilinear interp on every encode. ~12 GB total for the rbb corpus; converts the encode loop from I/O+CPU+GPU to pure GPU.

sections.body: Current encode path per shot: open_zarr → load uint16 (T,H,W) ≈ 89 MB → `_normalise_frames_to_uint8` (per-shot min/max scan + cast) → np.repeat to RGB → torch.bfloat16 cast → bilinear interp 536×560→256×256. The CPU/IO portion is ~0.4 s per shot. With 4 GPUs and a target encode time of ~3 s/shot, CPU/IO is 13% of wall. At larger batches or with longer rbb shots, this fraction grows. Precomputing once amortises the cost across every future encode AND the eventual training data loader.

Write to `/work/projects/imas_gpu/mast/preprocessed/rbb-256/<shot>.zarr` with a single 4-D array `data: (T, 256, 256, 3) uint8`. Per-shot bytes: 149×256×256×3 ≈ 30 MB → corpus total ~290 GB (9,527 shots). Fits comfortably in GPFS quota and stays compatible with `xr.open_zarr` for the encoding/training loader. Keep the original L1 corpus untouched.

New module `imas_ambix/data/preprocess.py`:

```python
def preprocess_rbb_shot(shot_id, src_root, dst_root, image_size=256):
    ds = xr.open_zarr(src_root / f'{shot_id}.zarr/rbb', consolidated=True)
    raw = ds['data'].values  # (T, 536, 560) uint16
    # Per-shot lo/hi (matches today's normalisation) so reconstruction is bit-exact.
    lo, hi = raw.min(), raw.max()
    u8 = ((raw - lo) * 255.0 / (hi - lo)).clip(0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
    rgb = np.repeat(u8[..., None], 3, axis=-1)  # (T, 536, 560, 3)
    # Resize on CPU once using cv2.INTER_LINEAR (matches torch F.interpolate bilinear closely).
    out = np.stack([cv2.resize(f, (image_size, image_size), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR) for f in rgb])
    zarr.save_array(dst_root / f'{shot_id}.zarr/rbb', out)
```

CLI hook: `ambix data preprocess-frames --camera rbb --image-size 256 --workers 16 --from-bucket-all`. Sharded across CPU cores on a `sun_debug` SLURM allocation (no GPU needed, just RAM + GPFS bandwidth).

`OpenMagvit2Tokenizer.encode_shot(shot_id)` gains a preprocessed-aware path: if `preprocess_root/<shot>.zarr` exists, skip the normalise/repeat/resize and go straight from `(T,256,256,3) uint8` → bf16 → daemon. Falls back to the legacy path for shots without a precomputed cache. Expected per-shot encode time after this lands: drop from ~3 s to ~1.5 s on H200 (GPU-bound).

Bit-exact reconstruction check: encode shot 15085 via (a) the legacy path and (b) the preprocessed path; assert identical token output. Throughput check: 100-shot encode wall time goes from estimated 5 min to estimated 2.5 min (2× speedup) on a single H200.

image-size.rationale: The frame tokenizer downsamples to 256² internally anyway. Storing at a higher resolution wastes space without gain.

normalisation.rationale: Existing encoder is calibrated against this normalisation. Switching to a global lo/hi or per-frame would require retraining/re-validating the LFQ codebook coverage.

questions.body: Use cv2.resize(INTER_LINEAR) on CPU or pre-load to GPU and use torch.nn.functional.interpolate? cv2 is simpler and saves the GPU for actual encode; F.interpolate matches the daemon's resize path byte-for-byte. Worth a 100-shot A/B for token-id divergence count.

followups.title: Implement preprocess.py + run on full rbb corpus
followups.body: Wait for zarr-consolidate to land first (depends_on). Then write preprocess.py + CLI hook, validate bit-exact on 5 shots, then sbatch a CPU array (sun_debug, 16 cores × 4 tasks) to chew through 9,527 shots. Total expected wall: ~30 min on 64 CPUs.

blocked_by.reason: needs consolidated metadata for the input reads

followups.est_turn: single Sonnet turn · ~2h dev + 30 min run

Plan: frame-precompute

Locked decisions to honour
  image-size      → 256
  normalisation   → per-shot min/max

Open decision to surface (do not resolve)
  q1: cv2.resize INTER_LINEAR vs F.interpolate (do a 100-shot A/B before deciding)

Done-when

  2. scripts/slurm/preprocess_frames.sbatch — sun_debug, --array=0-3, --cpus-per-task=16, --mem=64G, no GPU.

  5. OpenMagvit2Tokenizer.encode_shot gains a preprocessed-aware fast path (legacy path stays).
  6. data.impl → 1.0, status → shipped, plan §5 updated with measured speedup.
